{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), indicating market pessimism.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent price spikes — if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% after a spike, adjust next period’s forecast upward to avoid underestimating momentum.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast consistently overestimates true outcome over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period to align with historical mean.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is neutral (0.00) — avoid overreacting to minor price fluctuations.",
    "If true outcome is significantly higher than forecast (e.g., >10%) and sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.33+), increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33), adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect potential reversal or bullish sentiment.",
    "Avoid over-optimism in early periods — if forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–5% to prevent overshoot."
  ]
}
